label: Wave
short: A pattern that repeats in space and time and carries energy without carrying matter along, like ripples on water.

label: Frequency
short: How many times per second a wave repeats. Written with the Greek letter nu or f.

label: Amplitude
short: How tall a wave is, measured from its resting level to its peak.

label: Wave-particle duality
short: The finding that things like electrons and light sometimes behave like tiny lumps and sometimes like spreading waves, depending on how you look.

label: Photon
short: A single packet of light. Its energy is the Planck constant times the light's frequency.

label: Planck constant
short: A fixed number, written h, that links the energy of a light packet to its frequency. Its value is fixed exactly by the definition of the SI units.

label: de Broglie wavelength
short: The wavelength that goes with a moving particle: the Planck constant divided by the particle's momentum.

label: Quantization
short: The fact that some quantities, such as the energy of an electron held in a small region, can only take certain separate values, not any value in between.

label: Boundary condition
short: A rule about what a wave must do at the edge of the region it lives in, for example that it must be zero at a wall.

label: Node
short: A place where a wave is exactly zero. For a wave trapped in a box, more nodes means more energy.

label: Quantum state
short: A complete description of what is known about a quantum system, from which the chances of every measurement result can be worked out.

label: Wavefunction
short: A function, written with the Greek letter psi, that describes the quantum state of a particle. Its squared size tells you how likely you are to find the particle at each place.

label: Probability density
short: How concentrated the chance of finding a particle is at each point. Adding it up over a region gives the chance of finding the particle there.

label: Superposition
short: A state made by adding two or more states together. A particle in a superposition has no single definite value for the property in which the states differ.

label: Uncertainty principle
short: The rule that a particle's position and momentum cannot both be known exactly at once; squeezing one makes the other spread out.

label: Energy level
short: One of the separate energy values that a bound electron is allowed to have.

label: Ground state
short: The lowest-energy state of a system.

label: Excited state
short: Any state of a system with more energy than its ground state.

label: Degenerate
short: Describes different states that happen to have exactly the same energy.

label: Schrodinger equation
short: The equation that says how a quantum state behaves. Solving it for an electron in a given surrounding gives the allowed energies and wavefunctions.

label: Hamiltonian
short: The recipe for the total energy of a system, written as an operator. The Schrodinger equation uses it to find the allowed states.

label: Orbital
short: A wavefunction for a single electron. The shape of its squared size is the familiar cloud picture of where that electron is likely to be.

label: Quantum number
short: A whole number (or half-whole number) that labels a state, for example n, l and m for an electron in an atom.

label: s, p, d and f orbitals
short: Letters used for orbital shapes: s is a sphere, p has two lobes, d and f have more complicated lobes. They correspond to the values 0, 1, 2 and 3 of the angular quantum number l.

label: Spin
short: A built-in property of electrons that behaves like a tiny magnet with only two possible orientations, usually called up and down.

label: Fermion
short: A kind of particle, such as the electron, that obeys the Pauli exclusion principle.

label: Pauli exclusion principle
short: The rule that two electrons cannot be in exactly the same state, which is why atoms fill up shell by shell.

label: Coulomb interaction
short: The push or pull between electric charges: like charges repel and opposite charges attract.

label: Many-body problem
short: The difficulty that the motion of every electron depends on every other electron, so the equations cannot be solved exactly for more than a few particles.

label: Born-Oppenheimer approximation
short: The simplification of treating the nuclei as standing still while the much lighter electrons settle around them.

label: Electron density
short: How much electronic charge there is at each point in space. It is a single function of position, unlike the wavefunction of many electrons.

label: Exchange and correlation
short: The parts of the electron-electron interaction that come from the Pauli principle (exchange) and from electrons avoiding each other (correlation). Density functional theory has to approximate them.

label: Functional
short: A rule that takes a whole function as input and returns a single number. The energy as a function of the electron density is a functional.

label: Hohenberg-Kohn theorems
short: Two results showing that the ground-state electron density alone determines the energy and everything else about the system.

label: Kohn-Sham equations
short: A set of one-electron equations whose solution gives the exact ground-state density, if the exchange-correlation part were known exactly.

label: Self-consistent field
short: A loop that guesses the electron density, works out the potential the electrons would feel in that density, solves for a new density, and repeats until the density stops changing.

label: DFT (density functional theory)
short: A way of computing the energy and properties of atoms, molecules and solids from the electron density instead of the full many-electron wavefunction.

label: Periodic boundary conditions
short: A trick for modelling a solid: a small cell is repeated endlessly in all directions so that it behaves as part of an infinite crystal.

label: Unit cell
short: The smallest box that, repeated in every direction, builds the whole crystal.

label: Plane wave
short: A wave of constant size that ripples evenly through space. VASP builds its wavefunctions from many of them.

label: Pseudopotential
short: A smoothed stand-in for the nucleus and its tightly bound inner electrons, so that only the outer electrons need to be computed.

label: Simulation
short: A calculation on a computer that imitates a real system, so you can study it without building it.

label: Atom
short: The basic building block of ordinary matter: a tiny, heavy nucleus surrounded by a cloud of lighter electrons.

label: Electron
short: A very light particle with negative charge. Electrons around the nuclei decide how atoms bond and how a material conducts electricity and absorbs light.

label: Nucleus
short: The tiny, heavy centre of an atom, made of protons and neutrons. In most calculations here the nuclei are treated as fixed points.

label: Quantum mechanics
short: The set of rules that describes how very small things such as electrons behave. It replaces the everyday picture of tiny balls on tracks.

label: Approximation
short: A deliberate simplification that makes a calculation possible at the cost of some accuracy. Every practical method uses some.

label: Basis set
short: A fixed collection of simple building-block functions that are added together to describe a wavefunction or a density. A bigger set describes it better and costs more.

label: Supercell
short: A block of several unit cells joined together and repeated through space, used to model defects, surfaces or bigger arrangements of atoms.

label: Property
short: Anything you can measure or compute about a material, such as its energy, its shape, its band gap or how much it conducts.

label: Scaling
short: How the cost of a calculation grows as the system gets bigger. Cost proportional to size to the power 3 is called cubic scaling.

label: Force field
short: A set of fixed, simple rules for the forces between atoms, without any electrons in the calculation. Very fast, and only as good as the rules.

label: Hartree-Fock
short: A method that treats each electron as moving in the average field of all the others. It leaves out part of how electrons avoid each other.

label: Coupled cluster
short: A family of high-accuracy methods that add electron-electron effects step by step. Accurate for small molecules and expensive for large systems.

label: VASP
short: The Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package, a program that computes the energy and electronic structure of atoms, molecules and solids using DFT with plane waves.

label: Standing wave
short: A wave that does not travel. It stays in place with fixed points of no motion, like a plucked guitar string.

label: Normalization
short: Scaling a wavefunction so that the probabilities over all of space add up to exactly one.

label: Radial node
short: A spherical shell around the nucleus where an orbital's wavefunction is zero, so the electron is never found there.

label: Angular node
short: A flat or cone-shaped surface through the nucleus where an orbital's wavefunction is zero. The number of angular nodes equals l.

label: Electron volt (eV)
short: The energy an electron gains when it moves through one volt. The usual unit of energy for electrons in atoms and solids.

label: Angstrom
short: A unit of length equal to 10^-10 meters. Atoms are a few angstrom apart in a solid.

label: Band
short: A range of closely spaced electron energies that forms when many atoms are brought together in a crystal.

label: Band gap
short: A range of energies between two bands where no electron states exist. Its size helps decide whether a material conducts.

label: Density of states
short: How many electron states are available at each energy, per unit energy.

label: Hilbert space
short: The space of all possible states of a quantum system. Each state is a point, and adding two states gives another state.

label: Slater determinant
short: A way to write a many-electron wavefunction from one-electron orbitals so that swapping two electrons flips the sign, as the Pauli principle requires.

label: Spin orbital
short: An orbital together with a choice of spin up or spin down. Each electron occupies one spin orbital.

label: Correlation
short: The way electrons avoid each other because they repel, beyond what the simplest average-field picture captures.

label: External potential
short: The push or pull on the electrons that comes from outside the electrons themselves, in a solid mainly the attraction of the nuclei.

label: Ground-state density
short: The electron density of the lowest-energy state of a system.

label: Kohn-Sham orbital
short: A one-electron orbital of the stand-in, non-interacting system in Kohn-Sham DFT. Filling these orbitals gives the density.

label: Effective potential
short: The single potential felt by each Kohn-Sham electron: the nuclei, plus the Hartree repulsion, plus exchange-correlation.

label: Hartree potential
short: The classical electrostatic repulsion from the whole electron density, treated as a smooth cloud of charge.

label: Density mixing
short: Making the next guess of the SCF loop from a blend of the old and new densities, to avoid overshooting.

label: Residual
short: How much the density (or energy) still changes in one trip round the SCF loop. It shrinks towards zero as the loop converges.

label: Brillouin zone
short: The cell of reciprocal space that contains every distinct wavevector label k of a crystal exactly once, centred on Gamma.

label: Pulay stress
short: An artificial stress from an incomplete plane-wave basis when the cell volume changes; it shrinks as ENCUT is raised.

label: Smearing
short: Replacing the sharp step of occupations at the Fermi level by a smooth curve of width SIGMA, so that metals converge with fewer k-points.

label: k-point
short: A sample point in the Brillouin zone. VASP averages over a mesh of them to compute energies and densities.

label: POSCAR
short: The VASP input file with the cell vectors, the species, the atom counts and the atomic positions.

label: INCAR
short: The VASP input file of TAG = value lines that decides what is calculated and how.

label: POTCAR
short: The VASP input file with the PAW dataset of every species, joined in POSCAR order. Licensed; never shared.

label: OSZICAR
short: The short VASP log with one line per electronic step and one summary line per ionic step.

label: OUTCAR
short: The full VASP log: parameters used, symmetry, energies, forces, stress, magnetization and timing.

label: VASPKIT
short: A menu-driven helper program that writes VASP inputs and post-processes outputs.

label: job script
short: A batch file that requests cores and time from a cluster scheduler and starts VASP.
